note: Hand-derived from CanonicalObservabilityCoverageEdgeUpsertCypherFormat (go/internal/storage/cypher/observability_coverage_edge_writer.go): `UNWIND $rows AS row MATCH (obs:CloudResource {uid: row.observability_uid}) MATCH (target:CloudResource {uid: row.target_uid}) MERGE (obs)-[rel:%s]->(target) SET ...`, with the %s filled per row by canonicalObservabilityCoverageCypherType from the row's coverage_signal screened against the closed observabilityCoverageSignalVocabulary (alarm, composite_alarm, dashboard, log_group, trace_sampling) -- NOT from the port or family name. Each endpoint is a reducer.cloudjoin.CloudResourceUID value = sha256 over account_id, region, resource_type, resource_id, with account_id 123456789012 and region us-east-1 everywhere. Exactly five edges, one per vocabulary member: the orders-cpu-high alarm covers the orders EC2 instance (arn mode), the checkout-rollup composite alarm covers the orders Lambda (arn mode), the orders-overview dashboard covers the orders database by bare id (bare_id mode, proving the mode pin is not a vacuous constant), the /orders/api log group covers the orders queue (arn mode), and the orders X-Ray sampling rule covers the orders table by ARN dimension (arn mode; the classifier keys relationships by source ref alone, so a dimension-bearing relationship sourced at the rule's ARN classifies exact under the rule's own trace_sampling signal). The three restraints contribute nothing on purpose -- the metric-name-only alarm carries no dimensions (rejected, never fabricated), the checkout-service X-Ray match resolves by service name (derived provenance-only, never an edge), and the ghost-target alarm names an unscanned identity (unresolved gap, never an edge). coverage_signal and resolution_mode ride as Properties pins (the template SETs them as plain strings from the row); scope_id, generation_id, and evidence_source are writer-stamped per run and cannot be pinned statically.
